title: AutoTool: Dynamic Tool Selection and Integration for Agentic Reasoning
one_liner: Train an agent to choose useful tools step by step instead of assuming one fixed tool set for every problem.
lead: Many tool-using agents are trained under one fixed menu of tools. That works until the tool set changes, a new tool appears, or an old tool stops being useful. AutoTool treats tool choice as part of the task itself. It trains the agent to rank candidate tools at each step and to revise that ranking during a long solution because different stages of the same problem need different outside actions.

problem.h2: Why fixed tool menus break down
paras: A tool-using agent usually has two jobs. It must reason about the user question, and it must decide when an outside tool would add needed information or carry out a subtask. Many current systems train only the first job well. They assume the second job is simple because the available tools are fixed during training and testing.

That assumption fails in real use because tool sets change over time. New search tools, code tools, and visual tools arrive, and older ones may disappear or perform badly on some requests. If the agent learned only one frozen mapping from problem type to tool name, it cannot adapt when the menu changes.

callout.b: The paper's move in one sentence.
callout.html: Teach the agent to rank candidate tools during each reasoning step so that tool choice can change with the question and with the currently available tool set.

panels.title: 1. A question arrives
panels.viz_args: One request may need search, code, math, or image support
panels.caption: The request is not solved yet because the agent still has to decide whether outside help is needed.

panels.title: 2. The tool menu is large and changing
panels.caption: Several tools look plausible, but only a few are useful at the current step.

panels.title: 3. AutoTool ranks the options
panels.viz_args: Score candidate tools against the current partial solution
panels.caption: Tool choice depends on what the agent has already learned because later steps may need different support than early steps.

panels.title: 4. The chosen tool returns new evidence
panels.viz_args: Use the top tool, read the result, update the plan
panels.caption: The agent can switch tools after each result because one tool call may change what the next step should be.

panels.title: 5. The answer uses the right outside help
panels.caption: Performance improves because the agent is selecting tools as part of the solution process instead of following one fixed recipe.

steps.text: First train the agent to produce coherent multi-step solutions so that tool decisions are made inside a stable reasoning process.

steps.b: List candidate tools at each step
steps.text: Present the currently available tools so that the agent chooses from the real menu instead of from a fixed memorized list.
Order the tools by expected usefulness for the current step because only some tools help with the next missing piece.

steps.b: Call the best tool and update the trace
steps.text: Read the tool result and continue reasoning so that later choices can react to the new evidence.

steps.b: Train on many tasks and tool sets
steps.text: Repeat across diverse problems so that the agent learns a general tool-choice habit rather than one narrow rule.

paras: The paper changes tool choice from a fixed setup decision into a repeated decision inside the reasoning loop.

hidden.name: Expected value of each tool at the current step
paras: The key hidden quantity is how useful each available tool would be for the next step of the current solution. You cannot read that value directly from the question alone because usefulness changes as the partial solution changes.

AutoTool tries to estimate that step-specific value from the current reasoning state, the task type, and the available tools. That estimate matters because the best tool early in a solution may be a poor choice later after the agent has already gathered new evidence.

heat.caption: Darker means the system currently expects more value from that choice.

reads.html: The hidden quantity is which tool would help most right now because the current step has one main missing need and different tools fill that need with different success rates.
The method learns a ranked choice over available tools at each step so that tool use can adapt to changing tool menus and changing reasoning state.

mechanism.h2: Why this works: treat tool choice as a repeated ranking problem
paras: A fixed tool policy fails because the same question can move through several subproblems. Early on, the agent may need to search for facts. Later it may need a code runner or a calculator. A repeated ranking step works better because it lets the agent revise its outside help after each new result.

The second part of the method matters too. AutoTool does not only learn from final success. It is trained on long traces with explicit tool-choice reasoning because those traces show which tool was useful at each stage and why that tool fit the local need better than the alternatives.

stages.s: Rank available tools for the next missing step
Use one tool and read the returned evidence
Update the next ranking from the new state
Final answer with staged tool use

math.words: For each step, give every candidate tool a score from the current reasoning state and then prefer the tool with the largest score.
math.equation: score(tool, step) = fit_to_need(tool, step) + consistency(tool, step) - waste(tool, step)
symbols: overall value of choosing one tool at the current step
how well that tool matches the missing information or action in the current partial solution
how well the choice agrees with successful multi-step training traces on related situations
cost from choosing a tool that adds little value, delays progress, or sends the solution in the wrong direction

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: The agent must answer a science question with a missing numeric step.
Search tool: fit 4, consistency 2, waste 3, total 3.
Code runner: fit 5, consistency 2, waste 2, total 5.
The agent picks the calculator because the next gap is numeric and the other tools add less direct value.

math.note: The paper uses a trained ranking objective rather than this exact formula, but the formula captures the tradeoff the system is trying to learn.

charts.title: Fixed-tool or weaker tool-selection baselines
charts.note: These systems lag because they do not adapt tool choice well when the useful tool changes across steps or across tool menus.

charts.title: AutoTool
charts.note: The reported gains fit the paper's claim because dynamic ranking keeps tool choice aligned with the local need at each step.

items.html: If the right tool is missing from the available menu, the ranking step cannot recover because it can only choose among the listed options.
If the current reasoning state is unclear, the tool ranking can drift because the model no longer knows what local gap it is trying to fill.
A model may call tools too often if it learns that tool use is usually rewarded, so the waste term has to matter because unnecessary calls slow the solution.
The method is useful because it separates stable long-trace reasoning from dynamic tool choice, so the agent learns both coherent solutions and adaptable outside help.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a small benchmark with three tool menus that overlap but are not identical. Include math questions, search-heavy questions, and code questions. Run one agent that assumes a fixed tool mapping and one agent that ranks tools at every step. After each tool call, log the current step, the ranked list, the chosen tool, and whether the call reduced the next missing gap.

The demo should show higher end-to-end task success for the ranking system because the useful tool changes across steps and across menus. It should also show some success on unseen tools with familiar descriptions because the model is learning a choice rule, not only memorized tool names.
demo.closing: The core proof is that dynamic tool ranking keeps working when the tool set changes because the agent is learning how to choose, not only what it used before.
